The menu can now be hidden from recorders and screen sharing.

## New

- **Hide from recorders.** A "Hide from recorders" checkbox sits next to the theme selector, on the config page or in the pinned config group.
  - While it's on, the menu, and the toasts drawn over it, go into a separate window laid over the game. OBS, Discord, Snipping Tool and other capture can't see that window. To the player it looks exactly the same.
  - Display capture leaves the menu out. Window capture and OBS Game Capture only see the game's own window, which no longer has the menu in it.
  - Mouse and keyboard input work as before.
  - The choice is saved in `icarus.json`.
  - In code: `mod.setHiddenFromRecorders(true)`, `mod.isHiddenFromRecorders()` and `Icarus.canHideFromRecorders()`. `IcarusOptions.recorderToggle(false)` removes the checkbox.

## Limits

- **Windows 10 2004 or later only.** Elsewhere the checkbox isn't shown and the menu is drawn in game as before.
- **Not on 1.7.10.** Minecraft 1.7.10 doesn't ship JNA, which this needs; the checkbox isn't shown there.
- **Only the menu and the toasts over it are hidden.** HUD elements, toasts while the menu is closed, and Minecraft's own screen background (the dimming, and the blur on 1.21+) are still recorded.
- **It costs CPU while the menu changes.** The hidden menu is drawn on the CPU, typically a few milliseconds per frame while something animates. Nothing is redrawn while it's still, and dragging only moves the window.

## Also

- The skeet background draws about 80,000 fewer quads per frame. The pixels are the same.
- Headless snapshots no longer drop or double-draw pixels on quad diagonals.

```groovy
repositories { maven { url "https://repo.dreamys.studio/" } }
dependencies { implementation "studio.dreamys:icarus-<loader>-<minecraft version>:3.1.1" }
```
